What is the angle between two lines?

Two lines that cross form two pairs of equal angles: an acute angle θ and its supplement 180∘−θ. By convention, "the angle between the lines" means the acute one, between 0° and 90°. It depends only on the directions of the lines, not on where they are, so it can be found from slopes, from general-form coefficients or from direction vectors in space.

Try changing the input

Enter slopes 2 and −12. Their product is −1, the denominator 1+m1m2 becomes 0, and the lines are perpendicular.

What this calculator does

  • From slopes m1 and m2, with the tangent formula.
  • From general form A1x+B1y+C1=0 and A2x+B2y+C2=0, using the normal vectors.
  • From 3D direction vectors, with the dot product.

It gives the acute angle in degrees and radians, its supplement, and flags parallel and perpendicular lines.

The geometry behind it

A line with slope m makes an angle α with the x-axis where tan⁡α=m. Two lines with inclinations α1 and α2 meet at the angle α2−α1 (or its supplement), and the tangent subtraction formula turns that into slopes.

With vectors, the dot product gives the angle directly: u⃗⋅v⃗=∣u⃗∣∣v⃗∣cos⁡θ. Taking the absolute value of the dot product picks the acute angle, because a line has no preferred direction: u⃗ and −u⃗ describe the same line.

Special cases

Parallel: m1=m2, or u⃗ a multiple of v⃗. Perpendicular: m1m2=−1, or u⃗⋅v⃗=0.

Variables explained

SymbolMeaning
m1,m2Slopes of the two lines.
(A1,B1),(A2,B2)Normal vectors of lines in general form. C does not affect the angle.
u⃗,v⃗Direction vectors of the lines.
θThe acute angle between the lines.

Deriving the slope formula

Let tan⁡α1=m1 and tan⁡α2=m2. The angle between the lines is α2−α1, and by the tangent subtraction identity

tan⁡(α2−α1)=tan⁡α2−tan⁡α11+tan⁡α1tan⁡α2=m2−m11+m1m2.

The absolute value gives the acute angle. If 1+m1m2=0 the tangent is undefined, which means θ=90∘.

Why normals work too

The normal of each line is perpendicular to it, so rotating both lines by 90° turns them into their normals without changing the angle between them.

Complete worked example

Problem

Find the angle between lines with slopes m1=2 and m2=−13.

Step 1: Numerator and denominator

m2−m1=−13−2=−73,1+m1m2=1−23=13

Step 2: Tangent

tan⁡θ=∣−7/31/3∣=7

Step 3: Angle

θ=tan⁡−17≈81.87∘,180∘−θ≈98.13∘

Check

The inclinations are tan⁡−12≈63.43∘ and 180∘−tan⁡−113≈161.57∘. Their difference is 98.13∘, whose supplement is 81.87∘. ✓

Second worked example: lines in space

Problem

Two lines have directions u⃗=(1,2,2) and v⃗=(2,−1,2). Find the angle between them.

Step 1: Dot product

u⃗⋅v⃗=(1)(2)+(2)(−1)+(2)(2)=4

Step 2: Lengths

∣u⃗∣=1+4+4=3,∣v⃗∣=4+1+4=3

Step 3: Angle

cos⁡θ=49  ⇒  θ=cos⁡−149≈63.61∘

The lines need not meet: for skew lines this is the angle between their directions.

Practical applications

  • Road junctions: the angle at which two straight roads meet.
  • Trusses and frames: the angles between members, needed to resolve forces.
  • Optics: angles of incidence and reflection measured from a normal line.
  • Crystallography: angles between directions in a crystal lattice.

Common mistakes

  1. Dropping the absolute value. Without it you may get the obtuse angle or a negative angle.
  2. Calculator in radian mode. tan⁡−17 is about 1.4289 rad, which is 81.87°.
  3. Using the coefficients as slopes. The slope of Ax+By+C=0 is −AB.
  4. Treating 1+m1m2=0 as an error. It means the lines are perpendicular.

Assumptions and limitations

  • Slopes and coefficients may be fractions; the working is exact up to the inverse trig step.
  • Angles are shown to 4 decimal places.
  • Vertical lines have no slope: enter them in general form or as direction vectors.
  • Direction vectors cannot be the zero vector.

Frequently asked questions

What is the formula for the angle between two lines?

tan θ = |(m₂ − m₁)/(1 + m₁m₂)| for slopes, or cos θ = |u·v|/(|u||v|) for direction vectors.

How do I know if two lines are perpendicular?

Their slopes multiply to −1, or their direction vectors have a dot product of 0.

Why is the acute angle used?

Crossing lines make two different angles that add to 180°. The acute one is the standard choice; the calculator also shows the other.

Does C in Ax + By + C = 0 change the angle?

No. C only shifts the line; the direction depends on A and B.
